A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BigCodeBench and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated sections and v3's largely duplicated supplementary attachment can be matched reliably to v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations, tool-use analyses, contamination measurements, and human validation, including 32 successful solutions among 33 sampled tasks.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds benchmark correlations and a four-model evaluation of rephrased instructions.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, Complete-to-Instruct conversion, testing, and calibration procedures remain unchanged. Prompt rephrasing is an additional evaluation condition; BigCodeBench-Evolved in Appendix G.4 is a future maintenance proposal rather than a revision to the current method.

E1.justification: The correlation analysis adds MBPP+ and NaturalCodeBench's Python-English coverage. Appendix P adds evaluation under less structured, potentially underspecified instructions derived from BigCodeBench-Hard. The underlying benchmark's language, domains, and original tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Table 10 adds evaluated models Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, and GPT-4o-mini-2024-07-18 alongside the previously evaluated GPT-4o. Comparator membership in the retained main evaluations and chain-of-thought comparison is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix P introduces an original-versus-rephrased evaluation, using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct to rewrite natural-language instructions at temperature 0.2, with a reported top_k of 0.95. The existing zero-shot greedy and five-sample random-generation protocols remain unchanged; the latter parameter's labeling is unclear.

E4.justification: Appendix P adds a four-model sensitivity study testing performance under casually rephrased instructions. Appendix O extends the analysis of agreement with other benchmarks. Existing chain-of-thought, domain-level, contamination, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: There is no change to repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practices. The additional results use point estimates without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 10 adds original/rephrased scores, including 27.7/8.8 for Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct and 25.0/12.8 for GPT-4o. Table 9 adds MBPP+ and NaturalCodeBench correlations. The original detailed model scores and HumanEval+/LiveCodeBench correlation values are unchanged; the new prompt-condition results are not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Existing benchmark definitions and scoring mathematics are retained. The added empirical analyses and maintenance discussion introduce no new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions and central claims about complex instruction following, diverse tool use, and remaining model limitations. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive discussion of future contamination, limited annotator expertise and library diversity, and API-maintenance challenges. Appendix P qualifies the realism of structured instructions and acknowledges ambiguity from rephrasing; Appendix O explains NaturalCodeBench's closer alignment with Instruct.

D1.justification: Appendix P supplies the rephrasing prompt and generator settings, while Appendix N adds concrete visualization-test code. The cited artifact release changes from v0.2.0.post3 to v0.2.4, and dataset-hosting guidance shifts toward Hugging Face. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to SciCode, NaturalCodeBench, and two studies of Python API evolution or deprecation. These support localized discussion of benchmark coverage and maintenance; the principal research positioning and related-work sections remain stable.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized language corrections and clarifies calibrated Pass@1. It moves the benchmark-comparison section into Appendix O, adds appendix subsections, and removes the duplicated supplementary attachment while retaining its substantive construction guidance. Author affiliations and publication headers also change.

P2.justification: v3 Table 3 becomes the expanded v4 Table 9, with two additional benchmark rows. v4 adds Table 10 and visualization-test and rephrasing listings. Existing figures and main evaluation-table designs are retained, with limited layout and pagination changes.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly strengthens support for benchmark alignment and improves transparency through additional correlations, visualization-test documentation, and explicit coverage and contamination limitations. The rephrasing study is informative but limited: its example removes requirements, so the score drops cannot isolate sensitivity to wording. With the core benchmark and existing evidence retained, these additions support a limited overall quality gain.
